title: Errors and Error Classes
summary: throw, try/catch with unknown, custom error classes, and cause.

steps.title: Throwing and catching
body: if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 0) throw new RangeError(`bad age: ${s}`);
} catch (e) {                  // e is `unknown`: anything can be thrown in JS
else throw e;                // rethrow what you cannot handle
Built-in error types include `Error`, `TypeError`, `RangeError` and `SyntaxError`. There is one `catch` per `try` (no `catch (FooException)` filters), so you test the type inside it.
JavaScript lets you `throw "oops"` or `throw 42`. Do not: only `Error` objects carry a `stack` trace. That is why `e` is `unknown`.

code: console.log(e instanceof TypeError, e instanceof Error, (e as Error).message);
steps.explain: `finally` runs either way. A `TypeError` is also an `Error`.

steps.title: Custom error classes
body: Extend `Error` to give failures a type you can test for and data you can use:
this.name = "NotFoundError";        // shows in stack traces and logs
throw new NotFoundError("config", { cause: e });   // keep the original error
if (e instanceof NotFoundError) console.log(e.message, e.cause instanceof SyntaxError);
`cause` is JavaScript's `InnerException`. A common alternative in TypeScript is to **return** errors as values (`Result` types from module 5) for expected failures, and throw only for bugs.

steps.prompt: Match each situation to the best tool.
pairs: a value outside its allowed range
a domain error the caller will handle ("order not found")
an expected failure like invalid form input

steps.prompt: Throw an error, or return a result value?
items: the user typed an invalid email in a form
a function received `null` where the types forbid it (a bug)
the database connection string is missing at startup
steps.explain: Expected outcomes the caller must handle are values. Broken assumptions and unrecoverable situations are exceptions.

steps.title: Custom error type
prompt: Write `class HttpError extends Error` with a `status: number` field, a `name` of `"HttpError"`, and the message `"HTTP <status>: <text>"`. Its constructor is `(status: number, text: string)`.
- anything else that was thrown: `"unknown error"`
solution: if (e instanceof HttpError) return e.status === 404 ? "not found" : `server said ${e.status}`;
template: Dojo.check("is an Error", dojoE instanceof Error, "HttpError should extend Error");
hints: Test `instanceof HttpError` before `instanceof Error`: every HttpError is also an Error.

steps.title: Wrap with cause
steps.prompt: Write `loadConfig(text: string)` that returns `JSON.parse(text)`, but if parsing fails throws a `ConfigError` (write the class: `name` `"ConfigError"`, message `"invalid config"`) with the original error as its `cause`.
template: Dojo.check("throws a ConfigError", dojoErr instanceof ConfigError, "expected a ConfigError");
Dojo.check("cause is the SyntaxError", (dojoErr as Error)?.cause instanceof SyntaxError, "cause should be the original SyntaxError from JSON.parse");
hints: Pass `{ cause }` as the second argument to `super`.
